Definition: Flesh — the human body, human nature, and in Paul often humanity in its weakness and rebellion against God, apart from the Spirit.
BiblicalUsage: Sarx spans neutral (the Word became flesh) to deeply negative (the mind set on the flesh). Paul contrasts life kata sarka — according to the flesh — with life according to the Spirit.
TheologicalSignificance: Sarx explains the inner war every believer knows, and why victory is by the Spirit, not willpower. The Word became sarx to redeem sarx — flesh is not beyond His reach.
